topic: River with the greatest discharge: Amazon, average about 209,000 m³/s into the Atlantic — roughly one fifth of all river water reaching the oceans (Britannica; USGS). Congo about 41,000 m³/s (second); Nile about 2,800–3,000 m³/s despite its length (Britannica). Amazon length about 6,400 km from the Peruvian Andes; mouth more than 320 km (200 mi) wide; fresh water detectable far out to sea. In 1500 Vicente Yáñez Pinzón found fresh water out of sight of land off the mouth and named it Mar Dulce, the Sweet Sea (Britannica).
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: The Nile is the greatest river — it is the longest.
myths.reality: Length and flow are different records: the Nile carries about 3,000 m³/s, the Amazon about 209,000 m³/s — some seventy times more.

guardrails.why: Contested name — say 'the Gulf' or use both names (docs/BORDER_POLICY.md).
Sovereignty language on disputed areas is banned; say administers / claims.

screen_exempt: ^A was right|^B was right|^C was right

landscape.our_gap: River clips rank by length or argue Nile vs Amazon; nobody draws the river on the reveal, stacks the three discharge bars and rides a boat to the Sweet Sea on a moving map as a quiz.
